profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Lowest eval speedup of all 12 timing workloads (0.5302) and the shape the round-3 experiment plan targeted; attempted once at metrics level in the batch and once alone as a retry.
Highest absolute eval latency (85.14 us) of all 12 timing workloads; identical 16.7M-element geometry to timing-3 but bfloat16, making it the control for the 2-byte clamp hypothesis.
Second-lowest eval speedup (0.694) and 84.13 us latency; float32 4096x4096 kept the staged 8192-element path, so it marks the dtype boundary of the round-3 change.
Smallest workload (1024 elements), used as a fixed-cost control; also probed at instruction level to test whether the alternative collection path could produce artifacts.

performance_interpretation: Terminal outcome is failed: the service declares msprof profiling supported with metrics and instruction levels, but all six collection attempts returned zero artifacts with the same error, so no profiler fact exists for round 3 and no workload-scoped bottleneck is asserted. Using only the frozen eval comparison from get_profile_context: round 3 is PASSED on all 18 correctness and all 12 timing workloads with geo_mean 0.77130 (round 2: 0.74818, +3.09%). The frozen round-3 hypothesis (native-dtype saturating clamp plus a 16384-element tile makes the 2-byte 4096x4096 workloads memory-bound instead of tile-issue-bound) is supported for float16 (timing-3 83.44 -> 57.59 us, the largest gain of the round) but contradicted for bfloat16 (timing-7 85.12 -> 85.14 us) even though both are 2-byte dtypes taking the same clamp path and tile. float32 timing-11 is also flat at 84.13 us. Two eval-visible regimes coexist: the three 16.7M-element tensors, where dtype-specific device-side work dominates; and every workload at or below 1M elements, where latency is size-invariant and a fixed per-call cost dominates. Because the improved and unimproved 4096x4096 cases differ only in dtype, bf16 min/max lowering is the most probable localization, but it remains an unverified inference rather than measured truth.

next_experiment.action_description: Keep the round-3 structure intact (16384-element tile for 2-byte dtypes, 8192 staged tile for float32, float16 max/min clamp unchanged) and change only the bfloat16 saturation lowering: replace tl.minimum/tl.maximum plus the runtime .to(dt) scalar broadcasts with an explicit in-dtype compare/select chain using exact bf16 finite-limit constants (y = where(x > pos, pos, x); y = where(y < neg, neg, y); y = where(x != x, nan_v, y)), gated strictly on A.dtype == bfloat16. If timing-7 stays flat, the single follow-up probe on the same workload is a bit-level 16-bit saturation variant.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the bf16 clamp lowers the way the float16 clamp now does, timing-7 moves from 85.14 us (speedup 0.7294) toward the float16 result of 57.59 us, i.e. ~58-62 us, adding roughly +2.2% to headline geo_mean (0.7713 -> ~0.788). The other 11 timing workloads should be unaffected because the change is dtype-gated.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: bfloat16 compares may be emulated as expensively as min/max, producing another flat round for the cost of one experiment; bf16 limit constants must be exact and must not round through Python floats. Keep the dtype gate and the _ENTRIES/_try_build fallbacks to the validated staged kernel, and roll back to the round-3 source if correctness-6..11 (bfloat16) or timing-4/5/6/7 regress.
success_criteria: Full formal eval reports PASSED with all 18 correctness and all 12 timing workloads, including equal_nan, default NaN/Inf replacement and in-place same-object semantics.
timing-7 (bfloat16 4096x4096) latency <= 62 us, i.e. eval speedup >= 1.0, versus 85.14 us / 0.7294 in round 3.
timing-3 (float16 4096x4096) does not regress above 58 us and timing-11 (float32 4096x4096) does not regress above 84.1 us.
Headline geo_mean strictly above the round-3 value 0.77130.

warnings: No profiling evidence could be persisted as finding evidence: the service registers no downloaded artifacts for round 3, so findings is intentionally empty.

msprof collection failed on every attempt: 6 attempts over 4 workloads (timing-0, timing-3, timing-7, timing-11) at the metrics level plus 1 instruction-level attempt, all returning exactly 'msprof base collection exited successfully without profile completion marker'.

Every manifest (for example .kernelgen/profiles/round-0003/nan_to_num_-timing-3/a70395791b2a4f11b2a2d022dba13f0c/manifest.json) records artifacts: [], metrics: {}, capabilities: [] and summary.stage_count 1, so no performance counters, pipeline utilization, kernel report, or instruction listing exist for round 3.

The service declares profiling supported (profiler msprof, levels metrics and instruction, capabilities performance_counters/pipeline_utilization/kernel_profile/instruction_listing); this is a collection failure, not an unsupported backend.
Reproducing the same workload gave the identical error and the instruction level failed identically, so the failure is deterministic within this round rather than an isolated transient.

The candidate launch path uses a raw Triton launcher and deliberately bails out when enable_msprof_register_tensor or debug_enabled is set; whether that interaction can prevent msprof from emitting a completion marker is an untested open question, not a finding.

The frozen round-3 hypothesis can be neither confirmed nor refuted by counters; all comparative statements in performance_interpretation come from the frozen eval comparison, which is not profiler evidence.
open_questions: No profiler counters, kernel report or instruction listing exist for round 3, so no pipeline, bandwidth, tile-issue or instruction-efficiency claim can be made for any workload; all comparative statements here derive from the frozen eval comparison only.

timing-3 (float16 4096x4096) and timing-7 (bfloat16 4096x4096) share identical 16.7M-element geometry and the same 2-byte clamp path and 16384 tile, yet timing-3 improved 83.44 -> 57.59 us (-31.0%) while timing-7 was flat (85.12 -> 85.14 us). Does the bf16 lowering turn tl.minimum/tl.maximum and the .to(dt) scalar broadcasts into fp32 convert plus compare/select instead of a native bf16 saturating vector op? Only an instruction listing can settle this.

Every workload at or below 1M elements sits at 17.74-19.88 us across a 1024x data range (1024 -> 1048576 elements) with a roughly constant 2.8-4.1 us deficit against the reference. Is that a fixed host-side cost on the cached-entry raw launch path (dict-key lookup, _pick_block recomputation, stream getter call, 13-positional-argument launch) or a fixed device startup cost? The harness exposes no host/device split and the profiler produced nothing.

float32 timing-11 stayed flat at 84.13 us on the staged 8192-element tile and remains the second-worst workload (0.694). Is it limited by the same tile-issue cost the float16 path escaped, and would a larger fp32 tile help if the UB ceiling allowed it?

Why does msprof exit successfully without a completion marker on this workspace, and would a bounded debug job or a single-workload re-collection after the next candidate separate the profiler environment from the candidate launch path? The candidate deliberately bypasses its raw launcher when enable_msprof_register_tensor or debug_enabled is set, which is untested as a cause.
